facts: Movement speeds: WalkSpeed 396 cm/s, RunSpeed 654 cm/s, sustained empty-handed run/walk cycle 506.6 cm/s (docs/plan/economy.md:123); a cart moves at 297 cm/s (economy.md:135). The carrying slowdown f(weight) is still undecided (economy.md:125-126). The lead's 4.6 m/s figure sits between walking and the sustained cycle; I use 4.5 m/s below.

Night-length rule of thumb: night ≈ 160 + 5.3 × spine modules, where spine = BaseModuleCount × MainPathShare. It is fitted to only two points (henhouse 16/245 s, farm 60/480 s) and is described as a starting value to be tuned by play (docs/systems/stage.md:58-59).

SiteSizeCurve multiplies the module count from 0.85 on day 1 to 1.25 on day 10, while NightLengthCurve stays flat (docs/plan/data/progression.md:34-35). setup_stage.py already sizes the ground and NavBounds for the day-10 grid (Tools/Unreal/setup_stage.py:40-41,150-151).

Grid span is Clamp(ceil(sqrt(6N))*2, 16, 128) cells, at CL9SiteLayout.cpp:866 and mirrored in Python at setup_stage.py:79. A 200-module district is 70 cells (350 m) wide on day 1 and 78 cells (390 m) on day 10, because CellSize is 500 (docs/systems/asset-swap.md:252). Layout.Origin = (EntryOffset, -Span*Cell/2) (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:871), so the gate is on the west edge, centred.

Each Generate() call already carves its own entrance door (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:906-908) and one one-way flap exit at the deepest dead end (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:423-471, 969; module.md:190-195, the Lethal fire-exit analogue). A per-district gate and exit therefore come free with one layout per district.
Depth for Zones is normalised against the farthest hop in that one layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217). With one layout per district, zones are automatically evaluated per district.

Jars are placed one per delivery module of the layout (CL9GameMode.cpp:615-646). SpecialCopies applies per layout (CL9SiteMap.cpp:363). Depositing in a jar banks the item without walking it to the truck, and each deposit brings the blackout 4 s closer (docs/systems/raiding.md:26-27; docs/plan/data/rules.md:58).

Players still have to walk back to the truck: at dawn, any equipment item farther than EquipmentKeepRadius from the truck pad is destroyed, including items held by players (CL9GameMode.cpp:1149-1191, 1182-1186).

ACL9SiteMap is a singleton in practice. Find returns the first actor (CL9SiteMap.cpp:165-176), Rebuild and Clear act on that one (CL9SiteMap.cpp:178-230), and SpawnNight reads one SiteMap's layout and points (CL9GameMode.cpp:504-646). Other callers are GameState::RebuildSiteMap (CL9GameState.cpp:393-407) and the cheat LayEditorSiteMap (CL9Cheats.cpp:37-73).

SiteToWorld ignores actor rotation: it returns GetActorLocation()+(Local.X,Local.Y,0) (CL9SiteMap.cpp:238-242). The flap is spawned at GetActorLocation()+Spot with zero rotation (CL9SiteMap.cpp:465). ISM instances are added in local space (CL9SiteMap.cpp:504,549,567,786), so meshes would follow a yawed actor, but points and flaps would not.

The map is laid during the lobby, before the night starts (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212, 270-271), and at StartPlay (CL9GameMode.cpp:764-773). StartNight does not wait for the navmesh to finish building. The only nav setting in config is RuntimeGeneration=Dynamic (Config/DefaultEngine.ini:85-86).

Monsters are leashed to where they spawned: they wander inside HomeRange (CL9Monster.cpp:1123-1132), and chase breaks when they leave it (CL9Monster.cpp:1240-1241). HomeRange is 840 cm for chicken and pig, 1200 for raccoon and 2280 for goose (docs/plan/data/monster/*.md). Monsters never cross a yard, so monsters in unvisited districts never affect play.

Monsters do not set VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption; only the player character does (CL9Character.cpp:147). Performance budget is ≤ 4 ms of CL9 game-thread time (docs/systems/performance.md:18). Measured: 7 monster skeletal meshes ≈ 1.6 ms (performance.md:40). Each monster does one sight trace per player per frame (performance.md:118).

Farm zones total 34-45 monsters at base (Tools/Unreal/stages/farm.json:26-28) × MonsterCountCurve (0.6 on day 1 → 1.5 on day 10; progression.md:29). That gives about 25 on day 1 and about 60 on day 10.

Lethal Company comparison: indoor power caps run from 4 to 18 per moon and outdoor from 6 to 15 (docs/reference/lethal/lethal-map.md:195-206). Each creature costs 0.5-3 power (lethal-monsters.md:597-629). A day is totalTime 700 with startingGlobalTime 100, so about 600 s remain after landing (lethal-map.md:503-505).

Orders ask for about 2 orders of 1-3 cooked items per day (docs/plan/data/order.md:51-52, 89-91). The farm already spawns 40-50 eggs and 22-28 meat at base (farm.json:26-28), so what one night earns is limited by walking and carrying time, not by how many items spawn.

CL9.Map.LargeSite tests ModuleCount 200 over 30 seeds. It checks build, connectivity, overlap, one exit, at least 2 deliveries and at least 90% of the ground budget, and it logs ms per layout (CL9SiteLayoutTests.cpp:541-617). It does not test the day-10 count (250), the occupied bounding box, or spine length in metres.

objections.target: Equal 5 × ~200 module districts
objections.problem: This does not fit the 600 s walk budget for every district. The project's own formula gives one district a yard round-trip allowance of 600 - (160 + 5.3·0.3·N). For N = 200 that leaves 122 s by the base count (one-way yard of about 275 m at 4.5 m/s), and only 43 s on day 10, when 250 modules mean a spine of 75 (one-way yard of about 97 m). The grids are 390 m square on day 10, and with 90° yaw only two districts can sit right next to the truck (east and west arms, about 10 m). The north and south arms must be at least half a span away (about 195 m), and a fifth district at least about 300 m. So at least one equal 200-module district cannot be raided to its deep zone, and the far districts fail on day 10. The players' choice collapses to 'the nearest one'.
objections.alternative: Size each district by its yard distance. Per district: N_max ≈ (440 − 0.444·L)/1.59 by base count, where L is the one-way gate distance in metres (L=10→274, 100→249, 200→221, 300→193, 400→165), and divide by 1.25 for the day-10 worst case. Example totalling about 1,000: east and west arms about 230 each (L≈10-30 m), north and south arms about 190 (L≈195 m), one corner district about 160 (L≈300 m). Bigger near the truck, smaller further away.

objections.target: 'Districts further from the truck are the more dangerous/valuable ones'
objections.problem: If 'further' also means as big and as deep, the far deep zone, which holds the killers and most of the meat, cannot be reached and left again inside 600 s. The draft sets distance against depth when they compete for the same budget. Depth normalisation is per layout (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217), so a far district's 'deep' zone is only as deep as that district itself.
objections.alternative: Make far districts small and dense rather than big. Danger and value come from the zone composition (more pig, raccoon and meat rows) in a short-spine district. Data needed: an optional Zones override per district entry (empty means use the site Zones). A cheaper variant is one float per district (DepthBias) that shifts that district's points into the existing middle and deep bands. ValueRate stays at 1.0 because the economy is out of scope (stage.md:55).

objections.target: Arranging districts 'around/along an outdoor yard' without saying how they are oriented
objections.problem: The code cannot orient a district today. SiteToWorld drops actor rotation (CL9SiteMap.cpp:238-242) and the flap spawns unrotated (CL9SiteMap.cpp:465), so every gate faces west (CL9SiteLayout.cpp:871,889). With yaw 0 only, the districts have to stack in a north-south column 280-390 m apart. Gates 400-600 m away allow only about 100-170 modules, and the total falls well short of 1,000 (about 600-650 with 3 districts).
objections.alternative: Support yaw in multiples of 90° only, and treat it as required, not polish. Fix SiteToWorld to use GetActorTransform().TransformPosition, and spawn the flap with the actor's rotation; ISMs are already local and follow the actor. Lay districts out as a cross centred on the truck pad. Before placing the west arm, check where the existing food truck, kitchen and counter props sit in the duplicated level.

objections.target: 'Nav: open question whether tile count/build time needs navigation invokers or larger tiles'
objections.problem: Invokers are close to incompatible with decision 4 unless every monster carries one. They are also unnecessary: the map is built in the lobby (CL9GameMode.cpp:206-212, 270-271), so the dynamic nav already gets the whole lobby to build. The real gap is that StartNight never waits for the nav to finish, so on a short first lobby after StartPlay (CL9GameMode.cpp:773) monsters would spawn onto missing tiles.
objections.alternative: Build full dynamic nav over the union of districts with no invokers and no tile change. Gate StartNight, or at least log a warning, while UNavigationSystemV1::IsNavigationBuildInProgress() is true. Change tile size only if the measured build time is longer than a normal lobby.

objections.target: 'Rendering: per-district culling by distance/visibility; lamp count scales with districts'
objections.problem: One SiteMap actor per district already gives per-district ISM components, and the engine's frustum and occlusion culling then works per district at no cost. A new culling system is scope with no measurement behind it. The cost the draft misses is monster animation: all monsters stay active (decision 4), and 7 skeletal meshes already cost about 1.6 ms (performance.md:40). Around 100 monsters would break the 4 ms game-thread budget (performance.md:18) even though most are off-screen.
objections.alternative: Add no culling system in the first cut. Give monsters VisibilityBasedAnimTickOption = OnlyTickMontagesWhenNotRendered (or similar): AI, perception and movement keep running, which honours decision 4, and only off-screen pose evaluation is skipped. Measure lamps per district at 5×, and only then consider a per-district LampDensity.
objections.evidence: CL9Character.cpp:147 (only the player sets it); no monster setting found in Source/CL9/Monsters

objections.target: Monster count left as 'sensible vs Lethal' without a number (and the implicit 5 × farm)
objections.problem: Five times the farm is about 125 monsters on day 1 and about 300 on day 10, all active, and leashed (HomeRange 8-23 m) inside districts nobody visits. That is pure cost with no effect on play. The farm is already denser than Lethal: Lethal's whole interior holds at most 18 power (lethal-map.md:204), and creatures cost 1-3 power each.
objections.alternative: Treat one district as one Lethal interior, which fits because each district has one entrance and one fire exit (module.md:190-195). Give each district about 10-14 monsters at base, which is about 6-8 on day 1 and 15-21 on day 10. Total for 5 districts: about 35-40 on day 1 and about 90-100 on day 10. Near districts get lighter rows, far ones heavier. Treat the day-10 total as a ceiling to be checked against the measured game-thread time, not as a target.

objections.target: Yards as plain walking space
objections.problem: Monsters are leashed and the yard has no LevelPoints, so the yard has no content: every metre of it is dead, risk-free walking. The cart is worse at 2.97 m/s (economy.md:135), roughly 1.5 times the yard time. Equipment must come back to the truck or be lost (CL9GameMode.cpp:1182-1186), so players cross the yard twice.
objections.alternative: In the first cut, keep yards short; do not try to make them interesting. Place districts using the day-10 span plus a small road gap (about 10-20 m), and check each L_i against the formula above. Yard monsters or loot need a new spawn source (the flat-site ring at CL9GameMode.cpp:555 only applies when there is no generator), so leave them for later if playtests show the yard is boring.

objections.target: 'New MapTable row + level; QA ... and layout automation tests at the new size'
objections.problem: The generator is untouched, so a layout test 'at the new size' (1,000 modules) tests nothing new. What is new, and untested, is how districts are placed (overlap, yard distances) and whether a 230-module (day 10: about 290) district still fills to 90%. LargeSite only covers 200 (CL9SiteLayoutTests.cpp:551).
objections.alternative: Add one placement test: for the stage row, no two districts' day-10 grid rectangles overlap, and each gate's L_i satisfies the size rule. Run LargeSite at the largest district's day-10 count. Add AddInfo lines for the occupied bounding box (how much of the span the building actually covers) and spine length in metres, both computed from Modules with no PIE.

objections.target: Separate items needed for 'SpecialCopies per district', 'own yard_gate per district' and 'depth zones per district'
objections.problem: All three already happen for every layout: SpecialCopies at CL9SiteMap.cpp:363, the gate and flap at CL9SiteLayout.cpp:906-908,969, and depth normalisation at CL9SiteLayout.cpp:1201-1217. Listing them as design work makes the scope look bigger than it is.
objections.alternative: Drop them from the task list and note that they come for free with one layout per district.
